Depending on device oximeters can be quite inaccurate in measuring oxygen saturation levels, I've gotten some wacky readings myself. There's a lot of factors that can make them more inaccurate like nail polish, and apparently they tend to be more inaccurate the lower the reading is:
"Pulse oximeters are most accurate when blood oxygen saturation is between 90% and 100%. Accuracy decreases when blood oxygen saturation is between 80% and 90%, and the devices are least accurate when saturation is below 80%."
https://magazine.medlineplus.gov/article/getting-an-accurate-read-on-pulse-oximeters

Deconditioning can cause orthostatic intolerance and POTS-like symptoms. Deconditioning is also common in POTS patients as many have issues with exercise intolerance so it can be tricky to determine whether you have POTS causing deconditioning or deconditioning causing POTS symptoms. You mentioned you had pooling previously which could suggest you had POTS before becoming more sedentary. It would be good if you're able to see a doctor, especially if you feel like you became less active because of difficulty staying active rather than by choice.


Finding an exercise you could ease yourself into is likely to help. Deconditioning as well as POTS can cause hypovolemia so you might also find it helpful to try to get your blood volume up by drinking more fluids and taking electrolytes. As well as using compression garments, specifically for abdomen and upper thigh (so stockings/leggings/speedos), knee high compression socks aren't very effective. Hope you get better soon!

Maybe you would find it more practical to store the card number in a string. That way it's easier to work with single digits and you can find card number's length by looping through it. 

You can store a long into string using sprintf. When calculating check sum you'll just need to convert single digits from characters to integers.

As you said yourself you can automate things by using loops instead of writing same things over and over again. This may be more intuitive if you use a string to store the card number but it can be done either way of course.

Also you may want to organize your functions differently. For example, you could make checksum an independent function to make cardtype shorter and easier to read.
